chunks: Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda al-Kufi informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Mastoor al-Ashja'i narrated from his book in Safar of the year 266 AH, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ubaydillah al-Halabi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated from Amr ibn al-Ash'ath, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah Ja'far ibn Muhammad saying

while we were with him in the house, about twenty men. He turned to us and said: 'Perhaps you think that this matter of the Imamate is for any man among us to place it wherever he wishes; by Allah, it is a covenant from Allah that descended upon the Messenger of Allah to specific men, one after another, until it reaches its owner.'
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of the Imamate according to Imam al-Sadiq (as)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as) refutes the notion of *Ijtihad* (human choice) in appointing the Imam, asserting instead that the Imamate is a divine covenant (*Ahd*) transmitted through specific, named individuals. This establishes the principle of *Nass* (explicit designation) as the core mechanism of succession in Shia theology, ensuring the continuity of divine authority from the Prophet to the final Imam.
